## 債市主線

科技股再度遭到拋售，帶動資金轉向公債，美國經濟成長與通膨數據偏強也未能阻止美債上漲。2年期殖利率下降9.96個基點至4.5979%，10年期下降8.06個基點至4.9369%。Alphabet財報令人失望，衝擊從股票延伸至信用保險市場，投資人也調降對聯準會進一步緊縮的預期；同一時間，微軟$250億發債的認購訂單高峰卻達$1,150億。

這一日的市場更清楚區分了兩種意願：買進較安全的利率部位，以及出資支持企業擴張。美國投資等級與高收益債整體利差均明顯擴大。微軟受惠於少見的AAA級供給與強勁雲端業務成長，Broadcom與SpaceX的信用保護成本卻雙雙創下收盤新高。科技股跌勢雖重，並未全面波及股市；標普500指數逾400檔成分股上漲，顯示資金正從最受AI前景重估影響的企業轉出。

歐洲則有另一項政策變化。歐洲央行將存款利率維持在2.5%，總裁拉加德強調，目前能源通膨傳入薪資與基礎物價的證據仍有限。她同時宣布將於2027年2月7日卸任，接班競逐就此展開；若通膨前景未改善，官員仍準備在12月再次升息。因此，殖利率下滑之際，通膨風險依然存在，並非各央行已一致認定緊縮循環結束。

## 美債買盤壓過強勁成長與通膨數據

短天期美債領漲，延續前端對前一天聯準會暫停升息的反應。5年期殖利率下降9.43個基點至4.7428%，30年期僅下降4.3個基點至5.2996%。2年與10年期利差擴大1.9個基點至33.9個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大5.66個基點至70.17個基點。這次曲線趨陡是各天期債券同步上漲、短端漲勢較強所致，而非長端遭到拋售。

10年期殖利率下滑同時來自實質殖利率與通膨補償下降。TIPS實質殖利率下降4.44個基點至2.5871%，損益兩平通膨率下降3.62個基點至2.3498%。若拉長至一個月，兩者走勢仍有差別：實質殖利率下降30.69個基點，損益兩平通膨率卻上升0.68個基點。也就是說，週四通膨補償明顯回落，但過去一個月美債回升主要仍由實質殖利率下降帶動。

每週比較也顯示長端落後。2年期與10年期殖利率分別較一週前下降4.17與1.61個基點，30年期卻仍高出1.92個基點。過去一個月，2年、10年與30年期殖利率分別下降33.41、30.01與24.84個基點。公債回升之後，長短期借款成本的差距反而拉大。

當天公布的美國數據偏強，與債市漲勢形成鮮明對照。第3季GDP成長率初估為3.4%，高於市場預期的3.2%及前季的2.2%；實質消費支出成長3.8%，與前季相同。不過，GDP銷售成長率由2.8%降至1.7%。整體產出成長強勁，這項另列的銷售指標卻放緩，並非所有經濟活動數據都同步改善。

季度物價漲幅已大幅放緩，但9月數據顯示季末壓力仍在。第3季GDP物價指數上升2.2%，低於預期的3.2%，也低於前季的6.1%；季度PCE物價上升2.1%，低於預期的3.4%及前季的5%。核心PCE物價上升2.5%，雖由3.3%放緩，仍略高於市場預期的2.4%。這些季度數據與同時公布的月度指標涵蓋期間不同。

9月整體PCE物價月增0.5%，符合預期，較前月的0.3%加快，為六個月來最大漲幅；年增率也如預期由3.4%升至3.6%。核心PCE月增0.3%，與預期及前月修正值一致，年增率則由3%微升至3.1%。聯準會面對的是季度物價漲勢降溫，但年度通膨仍高於2%目標的組合。

9月家庭所得與支出則弱於預期。個人所得增加0.2%，低於市場預期及前月修正後均為0.3%的增幅。名目支出增加0.5%，低於預期的0.6%及前月的0.9%；實質個人支出在前月修正為增加0.5%後，本月持平。以購買力衡量的月度消費不如第3季整體消費熱絡，為原本強勁的一季留下較溫和的收尾。

勞動市場的失業救濟申請仍低。截至10月24日當週，初領失業救濟人數為19.4萬人，低於預期的19.9萬人及前週修正後的19.5萬人。截至10月17日當週，續領人數降至170.1萬人，低於預期的172萬人及前週修正值172.2萬人。另外，亞特蘭大聯準銀行將第4季GDPNow成長估值由3.3%調降至3.2%；這是新一季的模型更新，並非政府第3季GDP數據的修正。

BMO Capital Markets的Ian Lyngen認為，數據顯示通膨壓力持續，成長則在AI建設與消費之間呈現分化。TD Securities的Eli Nir與Oscar Munoz認為，經濟韌性不只來自AI，這也有助於解釋聯準會為何提高成長評估、仍持續關注通膨。依這些解讀，債市上漲與科技股衝擊、以及防範未來經濟放緩的需求關係更密切，而非已公布的GDP整體數字疲弱。

白宮國家經濟委員會主任Kevin Hassett在PCE公布後提出有條件的政策看法。他接受Bloomberg Television訪問時表示，若10月通膨非常高，可能就值得聯準會採取行動；反之，若通膨放緩，可能表示9月只是暫時波動。他希望看到10月CPI與PCE後，再判斷適當回應。這是白宮顧問的評估；聯準會理事Lisa Cook與克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack則已在週三會議中主張升息，投下反對票。

美國財政部7年期公債標售得標殖利率為4.894%，低於上次的5.085%。每週房貸利率也下滑，30年期由7.32%降至7.24%，15年期由6.68%降至6.60%。下午稍晚公布的聯準會週報顯示，10月28日總資產由$6.754兆降至$6.746兆，準備金餘額由$2.969兆降至$2.895兆。

股市走勢顯示，當天的不安集中在特定領域。那斯達克100指數下跌1.38%，費城半導體指數下跌1.42%，標普500指數僅跌0.30%，收7,720.39點；VIX升至17.2。美元指數下跌0.33%至101.854，黃金期貨也下跌0.38%，收每盎司$4,036.10。避險買盤最明確地流入美債，並非所有防禦性資產都同步上漲。

油價盤中一度因交易員評估與伊朗的外交接觸而走弱，收盤仍小幅上漲。WTI上漲0.08%至$102.86，布蘭特上漲0.44%至$115.83，後者仍較一個月前高18.40%。川普承認副總統JD Vance曾對外接觸，但稱那是提供醫療物資的提議，並否認曾指示重啟和平談判。盤中風險緩解之際，軍事風險仍未消除，能源收盤價格也依然偏高。

## 科技信用風險升高，微軟發債仍獲追捧

微軟在公布強勁雲端業績後，進行2017年以來首次美國投資等級債發行，直接檢驗市場提供融資的意願。公司分10批籌得$250億，天期從2年到40年；訂單高峰達$1,150億，為發行額的4.6倍，讓承銷商Wells Fargo、JPMorgan與UBS得以在行銷過程中收窄發行利差。

2066年到期券以較美債高1.05個百分點定價，最多較初步討論水準收窄0.3個百分點；評等較低的Alphabet之40年期債，次級市場利差約為1.33個百分點。微軟同時獲穆迪與標普給予AAA評等，美國上市公司中僅嬌生也有這項資格，加上多年未發債，使這筆交易有別於周邊供給。

不過，投資人對最長天期的科技業曝險仍要求可觀補償。微軟30年期利差為0.95個百分點，評等較低的寶僑本週稍早發行$12.5億30年期債，利差則為0.6個百分點。GW&K Investment Management的Brett Kozlowski認為，需求來自長天期AAA債的稀缺性及超過6%的殖利率；相較於承擔長達30年的商業模式不確定性，Wealth Enhancement的Ayako Yoshioka較願意持有微軟5年與7年期債。

微軟的財務結構也支持其借款能力。CreditSights估計，這筆$250億發債僅會讓經租賃調整的總槓桿比率略升至0.7倍。公司財報顯示，雲端營收成長48%，資本支出則受到控制；財務長Amy Hood表示，定價具吸引力時就會籌資。因此，這次融資有具體的營運與槓桿條件支撐，不只是仰賴科技大廠的知名度。

其他企業則因獲利前景重估而面臨更高信用風險。Alphabet的5年期CDS成本上升約5.1個基點至約84個基點，為7月以來最大單日基點升幅。根據ICE Data Services，Broadcom信用保護成本擴大約10個基點至每年175.4個基點，創收盤新高；SpaceX擴大約20個基點至266.5個基點，為今年稍早開始交易以來的最高收盤水準。

Alphabet搜尋與廣告銷售不如預期，尤其值得關注，因為這些業務是其AI投資的重要資金來源。新揭露的採購承諾、未來租賃及其他義務合計超過$1兆，其中約$985億為或有承諾，包括資料中心租金保證、支援合作夥伴購買電力設備，以及可能須向客戶買回AI晶片系統的義務。這些義務是否成為現金需求，取決於相關條件是否發生；但整體規模已讓投資人的關注範圍超出資本支出本身。

Impax Asset Management的Tony Trzcinka將科技業利差擴大歸因於未來發債量龐大及基本面轉弱，並指出自由現金流惡化、資本支出指引仍持續上修。S&P Global Market Intelligence的Gavan Nolan則強調債權人面臨的不對稱：AI若成功，股東可分享龐大上漲利益，債權人卻特別在意現金創造能力，以及支出何時能帶來回報。

避險市場也隨曝險擴大。巴克萊策略師Jigar Patel的分析顯示，截至前週，與10大超大規模雲端業者及晶片商相關的CDS交易額達$1,760億，為前一年的逾8倍。Oracle最活躍，交易量增至近6倍，達$468億。包括SpaceX在內的部分合約近期才開始交易，也擴大了市場規模及投資人的避險選擇。

銀行則另尋管道分散風險。匯豐先前曾評估市場對純資料中心投資組合的承接意願，目前正與保險公司初步洽談專案融資交易，其中部分涉及AI基礎設施；同時也在籌備一筆與逾$10億資料中心貸款相關的重大風險移轉交易。匯豐表示，這是正常投資組合管理，其曝險規模不大；與保險公司的洽談仍可能無果而終。

這些安排分配風險的方式不同。信用風險保險由貸款銀行支付保費，承保指定貸款約定比例的損失；重大風險移轉通常由投資人先交付流動資產，承擔第一損失層，並收取票息。兩者均可釋出監管資本、支援後續業務，但能否真正再利用這些承作能力，仍取決於有無願意承接的對手方。匯豐加入了分散AI曝險的銀行行列，保險公司是否接受則尚未確定。

企業整併也帶來新的潛在資金需求。Marvell正深入洽談收購Lumentum，後者市值約$830億，Marvell前一日收盤市值則約$2,200億。依Bloomberg交易報導，Marvell手上現金約$39億，可能高度仰賴股票支付。若完成合併，將把既有晶片與網路業務延伸至已用於連接AI系統的光學設備；交易條款尚未公布。另外，DoorDash同意以約$170億收購Instacart，以現金及股票支付每股$65；Thrive Holdings則同意以$76億現金收購ADT。

股市收盤後、美國固定收益交易時段結束前公布的財報，再度檢驗營運前景。亞馬遜第3季不動產與設備支出超過$770億，高於分析師預期，營業利益展望卻令人失望；英特爾因個人電腦處理器需求疲弱、資料中心零組件供應鏈出問題，營收預測低於預期。這些消息讓支出與變現能力的爭論，從Alphabet帶動的正常交易時段跌勢繼續延伸。

## 歐洲央行按兵不動，拉加德宣布提前卸任

歐洲央行討論了升息，最終仍將存款利率維持在2.5%，更重視基礎通膨穩定與融資條件收緊。拉加德表示，目前看不到超出既有預測、具重大影響的新增第二輪效應風險；政策聲明也指出，薪資尚未對能源衝擊出現明顯反應。

然而，9月整體通膨已達3.8%，油價比上次政策會議時高逾6%，天然氣價格則來到近四年高點。歐洲央行認為，融資條件收緊可能同時壓抑成長與通膨。拉加德指出，成長風險偏向下行，能源再度漲價正傷害消費信心，但未排除未來繼續緊縮。

市場定價略為提高、而非降低12月升息的可能性。決策公布後，市場押注的升息幅度一度達22個基點，相當於升息25個基點機率為88%，高於事前約80%；Bloomberg後續報導則將機率列為約85%。知情人士表示，官員認為若通膨前景未改善，可能仍需再升息25個基點，而中東局勢可能很快改變評估。

分歧在於緊縮循環還會延續多久。Bloomberg Economics的David Powell與Simona Delle Chiaie認為，央行強調能源外溢有限、金融條件收緊，是為結束緊縮鋪路，但12月仍可能升息；市場則還反映2027年至少再升息一次。這次按兵不動，並未消除各方對終點的不同看法。

拉加德為領導層交接訂下明確時程：她將於2027年2月7日卸任，早於原定2027年10月任期屆滿時間。她表示，希望能自由參與與現職中立要求不相容的政治事務，但未說明下一個職位；她先前已排除競選法國總統。

歐洲理事會主席Antonio Costa週四啟動接班程序，德國總理Friedrich Merz則表示，將在年底前作出決定。主要人選為現任國際清算銀行總經理、前西班牙央行總裁Pablo Hernandez de Cos，以及前荷蘭央行總裁Klaas Knot。De Cos在Bloomberg經濟學家調查中領先，並獲西班牙總理與主要反對黨支持；Knot獲荷蘭正式支持，也有領導金融穩定委員會的經驗。

遴選可能擴大為執行理事會職位的整體協商。Isabel Schnabel打算於2027年初提前離任、轉赴國際貨幣基金，首席經濟學家Philip Lane的任期則在5月結束，讓各國政府有多個職位可交換協調。拉加德提前卸任，也讓法國總統馬克宏得以在法國總統大選前參與選定接班人，為貨幣政策競逐增添央行獨立性的爭議。

消息並未立即引發主權債市劇烈動盪。Bloomberg最初報導中，德國10年期殖利率仍下跌1個基點至3.36%，法國對德國利差維持約154個基點；較晚的美國市場報導則列德國殖利率下降2個基點至3.36%，英國10年期下降3個基點至5.29%。法國財政困境仍是歐洲央行的重要背景，但週四新增的政策訊息，是利率不變、有條件的12月升息訊號，以及已有日期的領導層交接。

依Bloomberg轉述的法國公告，歐洲也宣布計畫釋出4,200萬桶石油。這項供給回應是管理能源衝擊的一部分，同時貨幣決策官員仍在評估衝擊會持續多久、如何傳導。

## 弱勢借款人面臨更嚴條款與稀薄流動性

歐洲高收益債中，強弱借款人的分化加深，評等最高與最低的非投資等級債之間，利差差距擴大至逾17年來最大。BNP Paribas Asset Management的Chris Ellis指出，部分困境債價格持續下跌，因為買方不願進場；EFG Asset Management的Mark Remington則表示，BB級債定價仍緊，規模較小的CCC級市場卻多以困境價格交易。

分化不只反映在價格，也改變貸款文件。為Platinum Equity收購雀巢飲用水業務股權提供融資的銀行，提高利差並加入涵蓋範圍廣的貸款人保護條款omniblocker，以吸引需求。Team.Blue撤回先前交易後，再次尋求債務展期，並提供定價讓步與保護條款；Paysafe也向債權人提供三項保障。相較之下，投資人視Intertek的檢測業務為較安全、類似基礎設施的資產，讓EQT為其安排的近£50億等值融資，以遠低於雀巢飲用水交易的利差完成。

其他市場也出現類似走勢。美國CCC與BB級債的利差差距較年初擴大逾一倍，來到2020年以來最大。巴克萊由Dominique Toublan領導的分析師團隊估計，AI投資等級債相對同天期投資等級債的利差分散程度為65個基點，高於一年前的24個基點。評等與產業內部的差距，說明大型發債成功與其他市場流動性受損可以同時發生。

Rovensa具體呈現了流動性困境。知情人士表示，本週有人折價求售其循環額度中的€4,000萬部位及約€2,000萬定期貸款，卻未能成交；限制嚴格的合格貸款人名單，壓縮了潛在買方範圍。這家由Partners Group支持的農業產品公司，在去年展期後，有逾€10億定期貸款及€1.85億循環額度，均於2030年到期；眼前壓力來自現金消耗與債權轉手能力，而非即將到期。

截至6月30日的會計年度，Rovensa自由現金流短缺€3,800萬，連續第二年為負，EBITDA則下滑15%至€1.44億。穆迪、惠譽與標普均已將其信用評等列入可能調降的檢視，面臨降至CCC級的風險。標普指出，巴西業務受穀物價格下跌與農業信貸受限影響，墨西哥則面臨關稅不確定性及農產品市場困難；會計年度末期，炎熱與豪雨也壓低歐洲施用量。穆迪認為，管理層的庫存及重要客戶措施仍有落實風險。

Cyfrowy Polsat選擇另一種降低槓桿的方式：專注媒體、電信與科技，計畫退出再生能源，並視出價情況可能保留少數股權。執行長Piotr Zak表示，淨負債對EBITDA須持續低於2.5倍，才可恢復股息；公司目標是在2030年前重建配息能力。公司預估至2029年，EBITDA每年下降2%至3%，之後才恢復4%至6%的成長；2027年因網路投資達高峰，將最艱難。股價一度重挫18%，反映去槓桿計畫伴隨的漫長配息等待期。

Lloyds財報則顯示高利率對銀行的兩面影響。第3季稅前獲利£23.3億，高於分析師平均預期的£22.9億，淨利息收入成長10%至£38億；但基礎減損費用增加78%至£3.13億，反映經濟前景轉弱與利率升高。公司維持、未上調指引，股價一度下跌6.2%。執行長Charlie Nunn仍形容信用表現強勁且穩定，但減損費用上升的情況並未因此消失。

中國方面，知情人士表示，珠海華發已向一項逾期信託產品的部分投資人還款。然而，其2027年到期離岸人民幣債週四上午仍約為面額的60%，一週下跌約38%；管理層也逐一會見債券持有人，試圖緩解付款疑慮。部分還款改善了其中一項義務，但集團融資憂慮仍在；旗下房地產公司另將第3季財報延後兩天至10月31日公布，未說明原因。

Shapoorji Pallonji正尋求由Eqyizen Investment增發盧比債，籌集$1.5億至$2億，約一半用於償還Porteast債權人，其餘償還集團其他債務。洽談仍屬初步，規模與條款可能改變，集團希望在11月中旬前完成。9月已借入約445億盧比支付分期攤還款，新融資將進一步減少Porteast債務、緩解其貸款成數壓力，但仍須與私募信貸提供者達成協議。

日本GMO則因另一種風險而遭信用重新定價。其2031年6月到期日圓債利差，由10月20日約122個基點，擴大至10月28日約174個基點，之後集團一家上市公司才揭露遭未經授權存取。GMO拒絕支付約¥80億贖金，並計畫賠償客戶損失，引發獲利影響疑慮。另一宗網路事件也干擾融資：Nissui因疑似未經授權存取導致子公司出貨中斷，基於投資人保護，延後原定¥130億5年期債發行。

## 政策傳導與主權財政比率的變化

日本央行決策前，2年期公債標售需求轉強。投標倍數由上次的3.89升至4.03，為6月以來最高，也高於一年平均的3.84；平均與最低得標價格差為0.014，與前次相同。BNP Paribas Asset Management的Ryutaro Kimura認為，高殖利率，以及法國債務疑慮、AI不確定性帶來的避險需求，共同支撐買盤。

這次實際標售結果，為近期日本公債需求回流再添佐證。週四隔夜指數交換反映12月日本央行升息機率約84%，而非預期週五就立即緊縮；投資人可以接受目前的短端殖利率，同時等待央行對後續政策路徑的評估。

紐西蘭央行總裁Anna Breman週四受訪時，更明確表示12月升息機率很高。市場反映12月9日升息25個基點機率為85%，多數經濟學家預期利率將達3%。在意外將利率維持於2.75%後，她重申需要評估第3季連續升息的效果，同時讓通膨回到1%至3%區間的2%中點。新的重點在於下次決策升息的可能性，而非推翻剛宣布的暫停升息。

印度財政部則強調，緊縮政策需要確實傳導。月度報告指出，印度央行近期升息的效果，將取決於是否積極管理銀行體系過剩流動性。依Bloomberg Economics，過剩資金已從9月初的11兆盧比，降至10月26日的4,620億盧比，期間央行先前也已升息25個基點至5.5%。財政部另列出聖嬰現象、節慶需求、原油高價及中東航運中斷等通膨風險。

財政部估計經濟活動仍強勁，但有所放緩：7月至9月成長率約7.3%，低於前季的7.8%；官方GDP將於11月30日公布。內需、投資與改革預料仍可支撐本會計年度其餘時間，因此政策官員須處理物價壓力，財政部並未預測整體成長將全面失速。

南非新版GDP計算，改變了主權財政比率的分母。南非統計局將基期改為2022年後，把2025年名目產出由7.6兆蘭特上修5.3%至8兆蘭特。PSG Financial Services經濟學家Johann Els估計，本會計年度總負債占GDP比率因而可能由78.2%降至74.5%，合併財政赤字比率由3.9%降至3.7%；財政部仍在評估影響，尚待提出自己的更新比率。

這次修正來自統計衡量改善與產業權重變化。礦業貢獻增加12.5%，部分因更完整納入非法採礦；金融、房地產及商業服務增加9.1%。統計納入的未觀察經濟占比由7.3%升至8.7%。這些變更擴大了用來衡量負債的經濟規模，並不是新宣布償債，也不代表當季成長突然躍升。

南非央行總裁Lesetja Kganyago另表示，央行模型顯示，最初燃料價格衝擊消退後，現行政策可使通膨回到3%目標。9月通膨為4.5%，政策利率在前月升息後為7.25%；他仍承諾，若通膨開始固著於預期、薪資與更廣泛定價，將採取行動。其判斷一方面依據模型認為政策力道足夠，另一方面保留有條件緊縮的準備，而非無條件預測利率不變。

美國有關以附買回操作為基礎的貨幣框架討論，則涉及另一種傳導問題。官員正研究能否更多透過貸款操作供應準備金，從而縮小證券投資組合。Warsh表示，資產負債表工作小組可能在明年初提出研究結果。美國銀行的Mark Cabana與德意志銀行的Matthew Raskin強調，這項方式有賴金融機構願意把央行流動性當作日常資金來源，而不帶有緊急借款的污名。

現行充裕準備金框架仍使貨幣市場利率保持穩定；若要改變，銀行行為與監管態度都須調整，增加隔夜融資使用也可能提高波動。這些操作條件是未來改革的一部分，尚非已決定加快縮表。同樣地，週四對減少聯準會每年利率決策次數的討論，焦點也是未來可能的波動：兩年期視野的波動指標幾乎未變，2027年9月至12月間的交換定價大致持平，儘管尚不確定秋季哪次會議將不再表決利率。

## 後續市場焦點

週五UTC 12:30公布的第3季就業成本指數，將在PCE偏強之後，直接檢驗薪資壓力是否持續。市場預期季增0.8%，前值為0.9%。UTC 13:45接著公布芝加哥PMI，預期56.1，前值58.8。強勁整體成長未能阻止美債上漲後，這兩項數據將分別提供勞動成本與地區活動的比較；聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem預定於UTC 16:30發表談話。

即使日本央行如Bloomberg調查所有經濟學家預期，將政策利率維持在1.25%，週五的評估仍很重要。若正式認定基礎通膨已達2%，市場焦點將轉向政策正常化的速度與終點。對買進2年期標售、同時仍高度押注12月升息的投資人而言，更新展望與總裁植田和男的說明，將影響後續判斷。

歐洲下一輪成長與通膨數據，將檢驗歐洲央行對能源高價與更廣泛物價壓力的區分。第3季成長率預期由0.6%放緩至0.2%，消費者物價漲幅則預期由3.8%加快至3.9%。官員打算依據12月預測作出下次政策判斷，這批數據將先於預測出爐；接班程序則有自己的時程，年底前選定人選，2月交接。

下週美國數據將擴大對需求與勞動市場的觀察。11月2日公布ISM製造業PMI，前值54.5，其中就業、訂單與價格提供不同面向；11月3日公布9月JOLTS職缺，前值707.9萬個。11月4日公布10月ADP就業，前值增加9萬人，同日ISM服務業PMI的前次整體綜合指數為54.9。這些各自獨立的數據，將檢驗第3季產出的韌性能否延續至新一季，並涵蓋不同雇主與服務業企業。

美國財政部將於11月2日公布融資估計、11月4日公布季度再融資公告，為11月3日期中選舉前後的借款前景定調。融資規模與到期年限配置，和選舉最終的政策後果是不同問題。近期短端殖利率降幅大於長端，使曲線更容易受到未來供給年限配置影響。

企業融資還有幾項更迫近、尚未解決的條件。匯豐仍須找到願意承接擬議專案融資曝險的保險對手方；Shapoorji希望在11月中旬前取得新融資，華發股份延後的財報則定於10月31日公布。微軟已完成的債券定價，證明市場對該發行人需求強勁，後續借款人仍須各自接受現金流、槓桿及集中度的檢驗。能源方面，在央行12月決策前，美國與伊朗的外交走向，以及軍事行動再起的可能性，仍足以改變燃料價格衝擊的持續時間。

overall_summary.headline: 科技股賣壓帶動美債上漲，美國成長與通膨偏強未能壓抑買盤
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Alphabet財報令人失望，科技股再現賣壓，投資人調降對聯準會進一步緊縮的預期，帶動美債上漲。2年期殖利率下降9.96個基點至4.5979%，10年期下降8.06個基點至4.9369%。短天期領漲，2年與10年期曲線利差擴大至33.9個基點。10年期走勢同時來自實質殖利率與通膨補償下降，兩者分別下滑4.44與3.62個基點。

第3季GDP成長3.4%、高於預期，9月PCE通膨年增率達3.6%、核心為3.1%，均未阻止債市漲勢。不過，9月實質個人支出持平，為強勁的一季留下較溫和的收尾。那斯達克100指數下跌1.38%，但標普500指數逾400檔成分股上漲，資金從對AI前景敏感的企業轉出。

美國投資等級與高收益債利差明顯擴大，Broadcom與SpaceX信用保護成本也創收盤新高。微軟$250億發債卻吸引高峰達$1,150億的訂單，受惠於AAA評等與強勁雲端業務成長。市場對微軟的追捧，與其他科技借款人的支出承諾及現金創造能力引發的疑慮形成對比。

歐洲央行將存款利率維持在2.5%，指出能源對薪資與基礎通膨的外溢有限；但若通膨前景未改善，官員仍準備在12月緊縮。拉加德宣布將於2027年2月7日卸任。油價盤中雖一度因外交消息而回落，收盤仍小幅上漲，能源通膨問題在下次政策決策前仍未解。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries rallied as a renewed selloff in technology shares restored demand for government debt, overcoming stronger U.S. growth and another firm inflation reading. The two-year yield fell 9.96 basis points to 4.5979%, and the 10-year declined 8.06 basis points to 4.9369%. Investors reduced expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening as Alphabet's earnings disappointment spread into credit insurance, even while Microsoft attracted $115 billion of peak orders for a $25 billion bond sale.

The session sharpened the distinction between demand for safer duration and willingness to finance corporate expansion. Broad U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads widened noticeably. Microsoft's reception showed the advantage of rare AAA supply and strong cloud growth, while protection costs for Broadcom and SpaceX reached closing records. The weakness in technology was substantial but not universal across equities: more than 400 S&P 500 constituents advanced as investors rotated away from the companies most exposed to the AI reassessment.

Europe supplied a separate policy development. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, with Christine Lagarde emphasizing limited evidence of energy inflation spreading into wages and underlying prices. She also announced her departure on February 7, 2027, opening a leadership contest while officials remained prepared to tighten again in December if the inflation outlook failed to improve. Falling yields therefore accompanied continuing inflation risks, not a shared central-bank judgment that the tightening cycle was over.

## Treasury Demand Overcomes Strong Growth and Inflation

Shorter Treasuries led the advance, extending the front end's response to the previous day's Fed pause. Five-year yields fell 9.43 basis points to 4.7428%, while the 30-year declined a smaller 4.3 basis points to 5.2996%. The two- to 10-year curve steepened 1.9 basis points to 33.9 basis points; the two- to 30-year gap widened 5.66 basis points to 70.17 basis points. This time, steepening came through a rally across maturities rather than a selloff at the long end.

Both real yields and inflation compensation contributed to the 10-year decline. The TIPS real yield fell 4.44 basis points to 2.5871%, and the breakeven declined 3.62 basis points to 2.3498%. The longer comparison remained different: real yields were down 30.69 basis points over the month, while the breakeven was 0.68 basis point higher. Thursday brought a meaningful daily retreat in inflation compensation within a monthly Treasury recovery still dominated by lower real yields.

The weekly curve comparison also showed the long end lagging. Two-year yields were 4.17 basis points lower than a week earlier and 10-year yields 1.61 basis points lower, whereas the 30-year remained 1.92 basis points higher. Over the month, yields had fallen 33.41 basis points at two years, 30.01 at 10 years and 24.84 at 30 years. The recovery in government bonds has thus left a larger gap between short and long borrowing costs.

The day's U.S. releases offered a firm counterweight to that rally. The advance estimate of Q3 GDP growth was 3.4%, above the 3.2% consensus and the previous quarter's 2.2%. Real consumer spending grew 3.8%, matching its previous pace. GDP sales growth, however, slowed to 1.7% from 2.8%. The stronger headline output result came alongside less acceleration in that separate measure of sales, rather than a uniform improvement across every activity series.

Quarterly inflation slowed considerably, but the September readings showed persistent pressure at the end of the period. The Q3 GDP price index rose 2.2%, below the 3.2% consensus and down from 6.1%. Quarterly PCE prices increased 2.1%, against expectations of 3.4% and a previous 5% rise. Core PCE prices increased 2.5%, slowing from 3.3% but slightly exceeding the 2.4% consensus. Those quarterly observations describe a different interval from the monthly releases that accompanied them.

September headline PCE inflation was 0.5% on the month, the largest increase in six months, matching consensus and accelerating from 0.3%. Annual inflation rose to 3.6% from 3.4%, also as expected. Core PCE increased 0.3% monthly, matching both consensus and the revised previous reading; its annual rate edged up to 3.1% from 3%. The combination left the Fed with slower quarterly price growth but an annual inflation rate still above its 2% objective.

Household income and spending were softer than expected in September. Personal income increased 0.2%, below the 0.3% consensus and revised prior gain. Nominal spending rose 0.5%, against expectations of 0.6% and a previous 0.9% increase, while real personal spending was flat after a revised 0.5% rise. The monthly purchasing-power picture was less buoyant than the Q3 consumption total, providing a more restrained endpoint to an otherwise strong quarter.

Labor-market claims remained low. Initial applications were 194,000 in the week ended October 24, below the 199,000 consensus and a revised 195,000 previously. Continuing claims declined to 1.701 million for the week ended October 17, against expectations of 1.720 million and a revised 1.722 million. Separately, the Atlanta Fed's Q4 GDPNow estimate eased to 3.2% from 3.3%. That model update concerned the new quarter, rather than a revision to the government's Q3 release.

BMO Capital Markets' Ian Lyngen described the releases as evidence of continuing inflation pressure and growth divided between AI construction and consumption. TD Securities' Eli Nir and Oscar Munoz saw resilience extending beyond AI, helping explain the Fed's stronger growth assessment and continued inflation focus. Those interpretations made the bond advance more closely tied to the technology shock and demand for protection against a future slowdown than to weakness in the realized GDP headline.

White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett added a conditional policy signal after the PCE release. He told Bloomberg Television that a very high October inflation reading would probably warrant Fed action; a slowdown instead could suggest September was a temporary fluctuation. He wanted both October CPI and PCE before judging the appropriate response. Hassett was expressing the administration adviser's assessment, while the Fed's two dissenters, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland President Beth Hammack, had already favored an increase at Wednesday's meeting.

Treasury's seven-year auction cleared at 4.894%, compared with 5.085% at the previous sale. Mortgage rates also declined in the weekly readings: the 30-year rate fell to 7.24% from 7.32%, and the 15-year to 6.60% from 6.68%. Later in the afternoon, the Fed's weekly figures showed total assets of $6.746 trillion for October 28, down from $6.754 trillion, and reserve balances of $2.895 trillion against $2.969 trillion.

Equities revealed the concentration of the day's anxiety. The Nasdaq 100 lost 1.38% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index 1.42%, while the S&P 500 fell only 0.30% to 7,720.39. The VIX rose to 17.2. The Dollar Index declined 0.33% to 101.854, but gold futures also slipped, losing 0.38% to $4,036.10 an ounce. Treasuries attracted the clearest haven response rather than every defensive asset rising together.

Oil had weakened earlier as traders considered diplomatic contacts with Iran, but finished modestly higher: WTI gained 0.08% to $102.86 and Brent 0.44% to $115.83. Brent remained 18.40% above its month-earlier level. Trump acknowledged Vice President JD Vance's outreach but characterized it as an offer of medical supplies and denied directing a restart of peace negotiations. The intraday relief therefore developed alongside unresolved military risk and elevated closing energy prices.

## Microsoft Finds Buyers as Technology Credit Risk Rises

Microsoft's first U.S. investment-grade bond sale since 2017 supplied a direct test of funding appetite after its strong cloud results. The company raised $25 billion across 10 tranches with maturities from two to 40 years. Orders peaked at $115 billion, or 4.6 times the offering, allowing Wells Fargo, JPMorgan and UBS to reduce the spreads offered during marketing.

The 2066 maturity priced at 1.05 percentage points over Treasuries, as much as 0.3 percentage point inside initial discussions. Alphabet's lower-rated 40-year bonds traded around 1.33 percentage points over Treasuries. Microsoft's AAA ratings from both Moody's and S&P, a distinction shared among publicly traded U.S. companies only by Johnson & Johnson, and its long absence from the market helped distinguish the transaction from the surrounding supply.

Investors still required meaningful compensation for the longest technology exposure. Microsoft's 30-year spread was 0.95 percentage point, compared with 0.6 percentage point on lower-rated Procter & Gamble's $1.25 billion 30-year sale earlier in the week. GW&K Investment Management's Brett Kozlowski linked demand to the rarity of long AAA bonds and yields above 6%. Wealth Enhancement's Ayako Yoshioka was more comfortable with five- and seven-year Microsoft debt than with the business-model uncertainty extending across 30 years.

The balance-sheet comparison supported Microsoft's capacity to borrow. CreditSights estimated that the $25 billion sale would lift gross lease-adjusted leverage only slightly, to 0.7 times. Its results had shown 48% cloud-revenue growth with capital spending kept in check, and Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said the company would raise funds when pricing was attractive. The financing consequently arrived with a concrete operating and leverage case, not simply the benefit of a familiar technology name.

Elsewhere, the earnings reassessment increased perceived credit risk. Alphabet's five-year CDS cost rose about 5.1 basis points to roughly 84 basis points, its largest basis-point increase since July. Broadcom protection widened about 10 basis points to a record closing 175.4 basis points annually, and SpaceX widened about 20 basis points to 266.5 basis points, its highest close since trading began earlier this year, according to ICE Data Services.

Alphabet's weaker search and advertising sales mattered because those businesses help fund its AI investment. New disclosures also exposed the scale and variety of future obligations: more than $1 trillion in purchase commitments, future leases and other obligations, including about $98.5 billion in contingent commitments. The latter included guarantees of data-center lease payments, support for partners' power-equipment purchases and potential obligations to repurchase AI chip systems from customers. Their conditional nature matters to when cash might be required, while the scale widened investors' focus beyond capital expenditure alone.

Impax Asset Management's Tony Trzcinka attributed technology spread widening to both heavy prospective issuance and weaker fundamentals, pointing to deteriorating free cash flow and still-rising capital-spending guidance. S&P Global Market Intelligence's Gavan Nolan emphasized the asymmetry facing creditors: equity holders participate in a large upside if AI succeeds, while debt holders are particularly sensitive to cash generation and the timing of the spending payoff.

The hedging market has expanded alongside those exposures. Barclays strategist Jigar Patel's analysis put CDS trading tied to the 10 largest hyperscalers and chipmakers at $176 billion through the previous week, more than eight times this year's earlier comparison with the prior year. Oracle was the most active name, with volume rising nearly sixfold to $46.8 billion. Some contracts, including SpaceX's, began trading only recently, contributing to the expansion of the market as well as investors' ability to hedge.

Banks were seeking another route to redistribute risk. HSBC was in preliminary discussions with insurers about project-finance transactions, some connected to AI infrastructure, following an earlier assessment of appetite for a data-center-only portfolio. It was also working on a significant risk transfer linked to more than $1 billion of data-center loans. The bank said this was normal portfolio management and that its exposure was small; the insurance talks could end without a transaction.

The proposed structures allocate risk differently. Credit-risk insurance involves a lender paying premiums for cover on an agreed share of losses on specified loans. A significant risk transfer generally brings investors' liquid assets in upfront against a first-loss tranche in exchange for coupons. Both can free regulatory capital for further business, but the availability of willing counterparties determines whether that capacity can actually be recycled. HSBC's approach added another lender to the effort to redistribute AI exposure without establishing that insurers had accepted it.

Corporate consolidation supplied fresh prospective capital demands as well. Marvell was in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, whose market value was about $83 billion, compared with Marvell's roughly $220 billion at the preceding close. With about $3.9 billion in cash, Marvell would likely rely heavily on stock, according to Bloomberg's deal account. The potential combination would extend its chip and networking operations into the optical equipment already used to connect AI systems; terms had not been announced. Separately, DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart for about $17 billion, paying $65 a share in cash and stock, while Thrive Holdings agreed to buy ADT for $7.6 billion in cash.

Earnings after the equity close added another operating test before the end of the U.S. fixed-income session. Amazon reported more than $77 billion in Q3 property-and-equipment spending, above analysts' estimates, alongside a disappointing operating-income outlook. Intel's sales forecast missed expectations amid weak PC-processor demand and supply-chain problems in data-center components. These releases extended the debate over spending and monetization beyond the Alphabet-led regular-session selloff.

## ECB Holds as Lagarde Sets an Early Departure

The ECB discussed a rate increase but chose to maintain its 2.5% deposit rate, putting greater weight on stable underlying inflation and tighter financing conditions. Lagarde said officials did not currently see a material additional risk of second-round effects beyond those incorporated in their projections. The statement likewise said wages had not yet shown a material response to the energy shock.

That assessment sat beside September headline inflation of 3.8%, oil prices more than 6% above the level at the previous policy meeting and natural gas at its highest in almost four years. The ECB said tighter financing conditions were likely to weigh on both growth and inflation. Lagarde described growth risks as tilted downward, with renewed energy increases hurting consumer confidence, while leaving the direction of future rates open to further tightening.

Market pricing moved slightly toward a December increase rather than away from it. During the post-decision response, wagers reached 22 basis points, equivalent to an 88% chance of a quarter-point move, from about 80% beforehand. A subsequent Bloomberg account put the probability around 85%. People familiar with the discussions said officials considered another quarter-point increase likely to be needed if the inflation outlook did not improve, with the Middle East situation capable of changing that assessment quickly.

The disagreement concerned how far the cycle would extend. Bloomberg Economics' David Powell and Simona Delle Chiaie interpreted the emphasis on limited energy spillovers and tighter financial conditions as preparation to bring tightening to a close, albeit with December still possible. Markets were also allowing for at least one additional increase in 2027. The immediate hold therefore coexisted with different views about the endpoint.

Lagarde's announcement established a firm leadership timetable. She will step down on February 7, ahead of the scheduled October 2027 end of her term, saying she wanted freedom to engage on political matters incompatible with the neutrality of her current role. Her remarks left her next position unspecified; she had previously ruled out running for the French presidency.

European Council President Antonio Costa began the succession process Thursday, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said a decision would be reached by year-end. Former Bank of Spain Governor Pablo Hernandez de Cos, now head of the Bank for International Settlements, and former Dutch central-bank chief Klaas Knot were the leading candidates. De Cos led the Bloomberg economist survey and had support from both Spain's prime minister and the main opposition party. Knot had formal Dutch backing and experience leading the Financial Stability Board.

The selection could become a wider bargain over the Executive Board. Isabel Schnabel intends to leave early in 2027 for the IMF, while Chief Economist Philip Lane's mandate ends in May. Those vacancies give governments more than one position over which to negotiate. Lagarde's exit also permits President Emmanuel Macron to participate in choosing her successor before France's presidential election, adding an independence debate to the monetary-policy contest.

The announcement did not trigger an immediate sovereign-market rupture. In Bloomberg's initial account, Germany's 10-year yield remained 1 basis point lower at 3.36%, and France's premium over Germany held around 154 basis points. By the later U.S. market account, the German yield was down 2 basis points at 3.36%, while Britain's 10-year yield was 3 basis points lower at 5.29%. France's fiscal difficulties remained central to the ECB's setting, but Thursday's new decisions were the hold, the conditional December signal and the dated leadership transition.

Europe also announced a prospective release of 42 million barrels of oil, according to the French announcement reported by Bloomberg. That prospective supply response formed part of the effort to manage the energy shock while monetary officials assessed its persistence and pass-through.

## Weaker Borrowers Face Tighter Terms and Thin Liquidity

European high yield showed a widening division between stronger and weaker borrowers. The spread gap between the best- and worst-rated junk bonds reached its widest in more than 17 years. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Chris Ellis described cases in which distressed prices continued falling because buyers would not intervene, while EFG Asset Management's Mark Remington said BB bonds remained tightly priced and much of the smaller CCC market traded at distressed levels.

The differentiation was changing documentation as well as price. Banks financing Platinum Equity's purchase of a stake in Nestle's water business increased spreads and added an omniblocker, a broad lender protection, to attract demand. Team.Blue returned to a debt extension with pricing concessions and protections after withdrawing an earlier transaction, and Paysafe offered creditors three safeguards. By contrast, EQT's almost £5 billion-equivalent financing for Intertek cleared at a much tighter spread than Nestle Water as investors viewed the testing business as a safer, infrastructure-like asset.

The pattern extended beyond Europe. The U.S. CCC-to-BB spread gap had more than doubled since the start of the year to its widest since 2020. Within AI investment-grade credit, Barclays analysts led by Dominique Toublan put dispersion against similarly dated investment-grade bonds at 65 basis points, up from 24 a year earlier. This separation within ratings and sectors explains why a successful large issue can coexist with impaired liquidity elsewhere.

Rovensa provided a concrete example of that liquidity problem. A €40 million portion of its revolving facility and roughly €20 million of term loans were offered at discounts this week but failed to trade, according to people familiar with the attempts. A restrictive authorized-lender list limited the pool of potential buyers. The Partners Group-backed agricultural-products company has more than €1 billion in term loans and a €185 million revolver due in 2030, following last year's extension, so the immediate pressure concerned cash burn and marketability rather than an imminent maturity.

Its fiscal-year free-cash-flow deficit was €38 million through June 30, the second consecutive annual shortfall, while EBITDA fell 15% to €144 million. Moody's, Fitch and S&P had placed its credit score under review for possible downgrade, threatening a move into CCC territory. S&P linked weakness in Brazil to lower grain prices and constrained farm credit, and in Mexico to tariff uncertainty and difficult produce markets. Heat and heavy rain also reduced European application volumes late in the fiscal year. Management's inventory and key-account measures remained subject to execution risk, Moody's said.

Cyfrowy Polsat announced a different response to leverage: concentrating on media, telecoms and technology while planning to exit renewable energy, with possible minority stakes depending on bids. Chief Executive Piotr Zak said dividends could resume only after net debt to EBITDA fell sustainably below 2.5 times; the company aimed to rebuild payout capacity by 2030. It projected annual EBITDA declines of 2%-3% through 2029 before growth of 4%-6% thereafter, with 2027 the most difficult year as network spending peaked. Shares fell as much as 18%, reflecting the distant payout horizon accompanying the deleveraging plan.

Lloyds' results showed the competing effects of higher rates on a bank. Q3 pretax profit of £2.33 billion exceeded the £2.29 billion analyst average, and net interest income rose 10% to £3.8 billion. Underlying impairment charges nevertheless increased 78% to £313 million, reflecting a weaker economic outlook and higher interest rates. The bank maintained guidance rather than upgrading it, and shares fell as much as 6.2%. Chief Executive Charlie Nunn described credit performance as strong and stable, an assessment that accompanied rather than erased the increase in charges.

In China, Zhuhai Huafa repaid some investors in one overdue trust product, according to a person familiar with the matter. Its offshore yuan bonds due in 2027 were nevertheless around 60% of face value Thursday morning, down about 38% over the week, while management held individual bondholder meetings to ease payment concerns. The partial repayment was a specific improvement in one obligation amid continuing anxiety over the conglomerate's financing. Its property arm separately delayed Q3 earnings by two days to October 31 without explaining why.

Shapoorji Pallonji was seeking $150 million-$200 million through additional rupee bonds issued by Eqyizen Investment, with roughly half intended to repay Porteast creditors and the rest other group debt. Talks were preliminary, with size and terms subject to change, and the group wanted completion by mid-November. The financing would reduce Porteast debt and pressure on its loan-to-value ratio, following September borrowing of about 44.5 billion rupees used for amortization payments. The new fundraising effort remained dependent on agreement with private-credit providers.

Japan's GMO supplied a different source of credit repricing. Its June 2031 yen-bond spread widened to about 174 basis points on October 28 from roughly 122 on October 20, before unauthorized access at a listed group company was disclosed. GMO refused an approximately ¥8 billion ransom demand and planned compensation for customer losses, raising concerns about the earnings effect. In another cyber-related financing disruption, Nissui postponed a planned ¥13 billion five-year issue after suspected unauthorized access disrupted subsidiary shipments, citing investor protection.

## Policy Transmission and Sovereign Ratios Shift

Japan's two-year government auction drew stronger demand ahead of the BOJ decision. Bid-to-cover rose to 4.03, its highest since June, from 3.89 at the previous sale and above the 3.84 one-year average. The gap between average and lowest accepted prices was 0.014, unchanged from the prior auction. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura linked demand to elevated yields and safe-haven interest amid French debt concerns and AI uncertainty.

The result added a realized auction observation to the recent return of demand for Japanese government debt. It came with overnight-indexed swaps implying about an 84% chance of a December BOJ hike in Thursday's account, rather than an expectation of immediate tightening on Friday. Buyers could therefore accept current short yields while awaiting the central bank's assessment of the eventual policy path.

New Zealand Governor Anna Breman sharpened her own December guidance in a Thursday interview, saying the chance of an increase was high. Investors were pricing an 85% probability of a quarter-point move on December 9, and most economists expected 3%. After the surprise hold at 2.75%, she reiterated the need to assess the effects of the third quarter's successive increases while returning inflation to the 2% midpoint of the 1%-3% band. The new emphasis was on the next decision's likelihood, not a reversal of the just-announced pause.

India's Finance Ministry emphasized implementation of tightening. Its monthly review said the effectiveness of the RBI's recent increase would depend on active management of surplus banking liquidity. Excess cash had fallen from 11 trillion rupees in early September to 462 billion rupees on October 26, according to Bloomberg Economics, alongside the earlier quarter-point increase to 5.5%. The ministry identified El Niño, festive demand, high crude and disrupted Middle East shipping as additional inflation risks.

Its activity estimate remained robust but slower: the ministry put July-September growth around 7.3%, after 7.8% in the preceding quarter. Official GDP is due November 30. Domestic demand, investment and reforms were expected to support the remainder of the fiscal year, leaving policymakers to manage price pressure without a ministry forecast of a broad growth breakdown.

South Africa's new GDP calculation changed the denominator of sovereign fiscal ratios. Statistics South Africa raised 2025 nominal output by 5.3% to 8 trillion rand from 7.6 trillion after shifting the base year to 2022. PSG Financial Services economist Johann Els estimated that the current fiscal year's gross-debt ratio could consequently fall to 74.5% from 78.2%, and the consolidated deficit to 3.7% from 3.9%. The Treasury was assessing the implications before issuing its own updated ratios.

The revision reflected better measurement and changed sector weights. Mining's contribution increased 12.5%, partly through better coverage of illegal mining; finance, real estate and business services increased 9.1%. The unobserved economy's measured share rose to 8.7% from 7.3%. These statistical changes improved the estimated scale of the economy against which liabilities are measured, rather than representing a newly announced debt repayment or a surge in current-quarter growth.

Governor Lesetja Kganyago separately said the central bank's models indicated prevailing policy could return inflation to its 3% target after the initial fuel shock faded. With September inflation at 4.5% and the policy rate at 7.25% following the previous month's increase, he retained a commitment to act against entrenchment in expectations, wages and broader pricing. His statement combined a model-based judgment of sufficiency with a conditional readiness to tighten, not an unconditional forecast of unchanged rates.

In the U.S., discussion of a repo-based monetary framework raised a different transmission question. Officials are examining whether more reserves could be supplied through lending operations, allowing a smaller securities portfolio. Warsh said the balance-sheet task force would likely present findings early next year. Bank of America's Mark Cabana and Deutsche Bank's Matthew Raskin stressed that the approach depends on institutions being willing to use central-bank liquidity routinely, without the stigma attached to emergency borrowing.

The current ample-reserves framework continued to keep money-market rates stable. A shift would require changes in bank behavior and regulatory attitudes, with greater use of overnight funding potentially adding volatility. Those operational conditions distinguish the prospective reform from a decision already taken to reduce the balance sheet faster. Likewise, Thursday's debate over fewer annual Fed rate decisions centered on possible future volatility: two-year-horizon volatility measures had barely moved, and swaps between September and December 2027 were broadly flat despite uncertainty over which fall meeting would lose its rate vote.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's Q3 Employment Cost Index, due at 12:30 UTC, is the next direct test of wage persistence after the firm PCE readings. Consensus expects a 0.8% quarterly increase after 0.9%. Chicago PMI follows at 13:45 UTC, with consensus at 56.1 after 58.8. The combination will add a labor-cost and regional activity comparison to a session in which strong aggregate growth failed to prevent a Treasury rally. St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem is scheduled to speak at 16:30 UTC.

The BOJ's Friday assessment matters even if it leaves its 1.25% policy rate unchanged, as all economists in Bloomberg's survey expect. A formal judgment that underlying inflation has reached 2% would shift attention toward the speed and endpoint of normalization. The updated outlook and Governor Kazuo Ueda's explanation will be consequential for investors who bought the two-year auction while continuing to price a high likelihood of December action.

Europe's next growth and inflation readings will test the ECB's distinction between expensive energy and broader price pressure. Q3 growth is expected to moderate to 0.2% from 0.6%, while consumer-price gains are forecast to quicken to 3.9% from 3.8%. Those results will precede the December projections on which officials expect to base their next policy judgment. The succession process runs on a separate timetable toward a year-end choice and February handover.

Next week's U.S. calendar broadens the demand and labor picture. ISM Manufacturing PMI on November 2 follows a 54.5 reading, with employment, orders and prices providing separate dimensions of the release. September JOLTS job openings on November 3 follow 7.079 million. October ADP employment on November 4 follows a 90,000 increase, and the ISM Services PMI that day follows a 54.9 headline composite. These distinct releases will establish whether the resilience in Q3 output extends into the new quarter and across employers and service businesses.

Treasury's November 2 financing estimates and November 4 refunding announcement will set the next borrowing outlook around the November 3 midterm elections. The funding quantities and maturity mix are separate from the election's eventual policy consequences. They arrive after a rally that has lowered short yields more than long yields, leaving the curve sensitive to the allocation of future supply.

Corporate funding has several more immediate unresolved conditions. HSBC still needs insurance counterparties willing to accept its proposed project-finance exposure. Shapoorji seeks its new financing by mid-November, while Huafa Properties' delayed earnings are due October 31. Microsoft's completed bond pricing establishes strong demand for that particular issuer; subsequent borrowers will face their own cash-flow, leverage and concentration tests. For energy, the direction of U.S.-Iran diplomacy and the possibility of renewed military action remain capable of changing the persistence of the fuel shock before central banks make their December decisions.

section_summaries.summary: Demand for government debt strengthened while corporate risk became more differentiated: U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads widened noticeably, but Microsoft attracted exceptional demand for its AAA bonds. The ECB's hold and Lagarde's February departure added a separate policy transition, with December tightening still conditional on the inflation outlook.

section_summaries.market_read: The curve steepened as short yields fell faster than long yields, not because the long end sold off.
section_summaries.section_title: Treasury Demand Overcomes Strong Growth and Inflation
section_summaries.summary: Shorter Treasuries led a rally despite 3.4% Q3 GDP growth and firm September PCE inflation. The 10-year decline combined lower real yields and breakevens; over the month, lower real yields still dominated the recovery. Flat September real spending tempered the growth picture, while technology losses were concentrated rather than market-wide and oil closed modestly higher.

section_summaries.market_read: Microsoft's strong reception coexisted with substantial compensation for long technology exposure and rising risk elsewhere.
section_summaries.section_title: Microsoft Finds Buyers as Technology Credit Risk Rises
section_summaries.summary: Microsoft's $25 billion sale drew $115 billion of peak orders, supported by rare AAA supply, strong cloud growth and limited leverage impact. Alphabet's earnings disappointment and spending obligations intensified concerns about AI cash generation, while Broadcom and SpaceX protection costs reached closing records. HSBC explored insurance and risk transfers for AI exposure; Amazon's spending and Intel's weak outlook extended the operating debate after the equity close.

section_summaries.market_read: The hold left the endpoint disputed: markets allowed for further tightening in 2027 despite arguments that the cycle was nearing its end.
section_summaries.section_title: ECB Holds as Lagarde Sets an Early Departure
section_summaries.summary: The ECB held at 2.5%, emphasizing limited energy spillovers and tighter financing conditions, but officials saw a December increase as likely if inflation failed to improve. Lagarde will leave on February 7, 2027, with a successor expected to be chosen by year-end. Pablo Hernandez de Cos and Klaas Knot led the contest, potentially linked to other Executive Board vacancies; the announcement caused no immediate sovereign-market rupture.

section_summaries.market_read: Strong demand for selected issuers can coexist with distressed pricing and poor liquidity among weaker borrowers.
section_summaries.section_title: Weaker Borrowers Face Tighter Terms and Thin Liquidity
section_summaries.summary: European high-yield dispersion reached its widest in more than 17 years, with weaker borrowers conceding pricing and lender protections. Rovensa's discounted loans failed to trade amid cash burn and a restrictive lender list. Cyfrowy Polsat tied dividends to sustained deleveraging, Lloyds reported higher impairments, and Huafa's partial trust repayment left financing concerns unresolved. Shapoorji sought refinancing, while cyber incidents affected GMO credit and delayed Nissui's issue.

section_summaries.market_read: South Africa's improved estimated debt ratio reflects a larger measured economy, rather than a newly announced debt repayment.
section_summaries.section_title: Policy Transmission and Sovereign Ratios Shift
section_summaries.summary: Japan's 2-year auction drew stronger demand ahead of the BOJ decision, while New Zealand signaled a high chance of a December increase and India stressed liquidity management to transmit tightening. South Africa's GDP rebasing enlarged the fiscal denominator; lower debt-ratio estimates came from an economist while Treasury assessed the effects. U.S. officials explored a repo-based framework whose viability depends on routine bank use of central-bank liquidity.

Friday's U.S. wage-cost data and the BOJ outlook test inflation persistence and normalization, while European growth and inflation releases inform December policy. Next week's U.S. activity and labor data broaden the growth picture; Treasury financing estimates and refunding details test supply sensitivity after the curve steepened. Corporate refinancing, HSBC's search for insurance counterparties and U.S.-Iran developments remain unresolved.

overall_summary.headline: Technology selloff drives a Treasury rally despite firm U.S. growth and inflation
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries rallied as Alphabet's earnings disappointment renewed selling in technology shares and investors reduced expectations for further Fed tightening. The 2-year yield fell 9.96 basis points to 4.5979%, while the 10-year declined 8.06 basis points to 4.9369%. Short maturities led the advance, steepening the 2- to 10-year curve to 33.9 basis points. Lower real yields and inflation compensation both contributed to the 10-year move, falling 4.44 and 3.62 basis points respectively.

The rally overcame Q3 GDP growth of 3.4%, above expectations, and September PCE inflation of 3.6% annually, with core inflation at 3.1%. Flat real personal spending in September offered a softer endpoint to the strong quarter. The Nasdaq 100 fell 1.38%, but more than 400 S&P 500 constituents advanced as investors rotated away from AI-sensitive companies.

U.S. investment-grade and high-yield spreads widened noticeably, while Broadcom and SpaceX credit-protection costs reached closing records. Microsoft's $25 billion bond sale nevertheless drew $115 billion of peak orders, supported by its AAA ratings and strong cloud growth. Its reception contrasted with rising concern about other technology borrowers' spending commitments and cash generation.

The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.5%, citing limited energy spillovers into wages and underlying inflation, while officials remained prepared to tighten in December if the inflation outlook failed to improve. Christine Lagarde announced she would step down on February 7, 2027. Oil finished modestly higher despite earlier diplomatic relief, leaving energy inflation unresolved ahead of the next policy decisions.
overall_summary.summary: Demand for safer government debt accompanied noticeably wider U.S. credit spreads, even as Microsoft's rare AAA offering attracted strong demand and the ECB kept a December rate increase in view.
